transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 09:34 UTC
Duration: ~55 mins
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jules (Redwood SE), Maya (Lorch), Evan (Lorch), Priya (Lorch)

Summary: quick POC scoping focused on benchmark harness onramp, customer scripts integration, streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, and success criteria for SLA. High level agreement to run a short handshake run then a 2-3 day soak with fallthrough routing enabled.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, harness adapter, streaming vs batch, KV cache warmup, tail latency targets, fallthrough to cheaper model, security/peering.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round — can we state roles?
[00:05] Maya: Maya, lead ML eng, running the recommender infra and the inference stack.
[00:10] Evan: Evan, platform, I own VPCs and test infra.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, product — I'm watching SLOs and business impact.
[00:18] Samir: Great. Jules from our SE team will run thru the harness steps. Jules over to you.
[00:24] Jules: Cool, thanks. So goal: get your customer scripts integrated into our benchmark harness, run streaming and non-streaming profiles, and measure throughput, p95/p99 latency, and token cost. We'll do a handshake run then scale.
[00:40] Maya: sounds good. couple clarifying points: our production prompts are a mix — short 20-token prompts for nav, and long form multi-turn of liike 400 tokens for summaries. Also some conversation state so KV cache matters.
[00:56] Jules: perfect. that's the common pattern we see. for the harness we ask for a 2 hour representative sample and 10-20 long tail prompts. we use that to synthesize load shapes: steady, spike, and ramp.
[01:10] Evan: question — we plan to use private early POC in our AWS VPC, is that supported for handshake? what about IP allowlist?
[01:18] Samir: yes, we can do Private mode with a temporary peering; if you can't do peering we can also run a hosted handshake and restrict by API key. Evan: we'll check with security.
[01:29] Maya: success criteria from our side: 1) p95 latency under 350ms for short prompts at 75% load, 2) throughput scale to 400 qps for short prompts, 3) error rate <0.5% sustained. if we degrade more than 10% of quality we fail.
[01:50] Priya: and for cost, we want a ballpark per-1M token cost to compare to our current infra.
[01:58] Jules: we'll surface token-level cost and a delta for streaming vs non-streaming. note streaming often reduces latency for early tokens but can increase overall resource overhead — depends on your client and average response length.
[02:20] Samir: quick note on fallthrough: we recommend enabling a cheaper model variant for backfill during spikes. the harness will exercise fallthrough rules so you see both perf and functional differences.
[02:33] Evan: what about KV cache warmup? our workload has many repeated prefixes. cold start latency is a concern.
[02:40] Jules: we have two knobs: pre-warm the KV cache by replaying representative traffic and run a warmup phase in the harness. also we provide a K-V cache heatmap as part of telemetry so you can see warm/cold token ratios.
[02:56] Maya: telemetry — will we get traces per request? we need per-route breakdowns for our product dashboards.
[03:03] Jules: yes, the console includes per-route latency, token counts, and tracing hooks. for the POC we'll share a dashboard link and a CSV export.
[03:12] Samir: ok let's step through the harness onboarding steps briefly — Jules?
[03:16] Jules: step 1: share sample traffic (CSV or ndjson) with prompts + metadata. step 2: we provide an adapter scaffold (Python + Go examples) to map your client calls to the harness. step 3: handshake run: smoke test then 30min steady at low qps, step 4: scale tests — 1hr ramp/1hr steady/soak. we'll run streaming and non-streaming profiles back-to-back so you can compare.
[03:42] Maya: how intrusive is the adapter change? we have a proprietary client library.
[03:46] Jules: adapter is thin: you implement a send_request(payload) and a callback to parse streaming frames if you use streaming. we can do a proxy mode where you don't change client by mirroring traffic — but that requires network mirroring which may be heavier.
[04:02] Evan: would we be able to run the harness from our CI? or does Redwood host the harness?
[04:07] Jules: both. we have a hosted harness option for quick runs, or you can run the harness in your CI; the adapter just needs to point at the target endpoint. CI-run is preferred for private deployments.
[04:19] Maya: perf targets — can we set a realistic p95 for long prompts? our long prompts are more tolerant, p95 ~1.5s acceptable but cost matters.
[04:28] Samir: yes, we should split targets by prompt class: short p95 <350ms, medium (100-300 tokens) p95 <700ms, long (300+ tokens) p95 <1.5s. we'll document in acceptance criteria.
[04:40] Priya: acceptance criteria also needs to include quality checks — we have a small eval set to detect regressions.
[04:46] Jules: absolutely. include your eval prompts in the harness. we'll run a QA pass and surface BLEU/ROUGE-like scores or embedding similarity diffs. if regression >X% we flag it.
[04:59] Evan: streaming vs non-streaming — what are the typical tradeoffs we should expect?
[05:03] Jules: streaming gives earlier first-byte latency which helps perceived latency, and reduces tail for short responses. however it can increase resource usage due to more frequent network operations and can complicate client logic (reconnects, frame reassembly). Non-streaming (batch) tends to be simpler and sometimes slightly cheaper for long outputs because the runtime can pack tokens more efficiently. we'll quantify both on your traffic.
[05:31] Maya: we also have an X-throughput SLA at peak hours, and need graceful degradation — what does Redwood's fallthrough look like?
[05:38] Samir: fallthrough is policy-driven: route to cheaper model variant or alternate region, can throttle with queueing or reject. for the POC we'll test a policy that routes 20% to fallback during a spike to measure quality loss and cost savings.
[05:56] Priya: security questions again — do you support bring-your-own-KMS for private? and audit logs?
[06:02] Samir: yes BYOK supported for Private deployments and you get audit logs with per-request metadata. we'll drop the SOC2 snapshot and the KMS integration guide in the shared folder.
[06:12] Maya: any gotchas we should be aware of for the harness when we have multi-turn state?
[06:17] Jules: keep conversation state in your adapter so the harness can supply prefixes for streaming vs non-streaming. also ensure tokens-per-second distribution is represented — otherwise batching looks better than reality.
[06:29] Evan: about metrics — we'll need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency. will the harness give us a CSV?
[06:36] Jules: yes, we export a per-request CSV with timestamps, model variant, tokens_in/tokens_out, latency_ms, error_code, and which routing policy applied.
[06:47] Maya: great. what about warmup timing? if we pre-warm KV cache for repeated prefixes, how long before we consider warmed?
[06:54] Jules: depends on your repeat factor. typical rule: 10-20 repeats of key prefixes to reach steady-state for cache hit rates. the harvest will show hit ratio over time.
[07:05] Samir: wrap-up on scheduling: we propose handshake week of July 6th. initial run: hosted smoke then private handshake once peering confirmed.
[07:13] Priya: timeline for evaluation: 2 weeks for POC including 2-3 day soak after initial runs, then a review and decision.
[07:20] Samir: noted. any other open concerns?
[07:23] Maya: regression detection thresholds — what's typical?
[07:25] Jules: teams usually set a relative quality regression threshold of 2-3% on embedding similarity or 5% on exact-match metrics; we'll let you pick which metric.
[07:36] Evan: one more — can we test cold-start tail latency? we need cold-start numbers for bursty traffic.
[07:40] Jules: yes the harness can run cold-start experiments by spinning up empty instances and firing a ramp, capturing cold tail. we also capture cold vs warm breakdown.
[07:51] Samir: okay I'll follow up with pricing and enterprise options. Jules will share harness artifacts. Maya/Evan to provide data samples and confirm peering.
[07:59] Priya: can you also include a sample SLA doc for dedicated capacity?
[08:03] Samir: yes, will include SLA excerpt.
[08:06] (brief cross talk, actions repeated)
[08:15] End
